title: Dynamic per-customer rate limits, tiered quota buckets, and soft-overage grace policy PRD
creator: Mariana Costa
description: Problem: Fixed, plan-level quotas and single hard limits cause poor UX for bursty workloads, manual support escalations for short spikes, and lost revenue from conservative hard caps. Goal: Implement a flexible, per-customer rate-limiting and quota system with tiered quota buckets (daily/weekly/monthly), configurable burst capacity, and a soft-overage grace policy that allows short-term overages to proceed while ensuring predictable billing and clear observability. This ticket captures product requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout constraints, and handoffs for engineering, billing, and console teams.
requirements: Support per-customer quota configuration: plan defaults + customer overrides (daily, weekly, monthly units and burst capacity)
Expose dynamic rate-limit headers in API responses (X-RW-Quota-Remaining, X-RW-Quota-Reset, X-RW-Burst-Remaining, X-RW-Overage-State)

Enforcement model: token-bucket per (customer, route) with configurable burst tokens and refill intervals; soft-overage allows requests beyond quota for a configurable grace window before billing trigger or hard throttle
Soft-overage policy: configurable grace window (default 24 hours) per plan; overage recorded as ledger events but requests still served until grace expires or threshold exceeded
Billing integration: generate signed overage events to billing pipeline (Kafka topic: billing.overages) with metadata (customer_id, plan_id, usage_units, window_start, window_end, overage_reason)
Console: new quota management UI for customer overrides and a per-customer usage timeline that highlights soft-overage windows and projected charges
Notifications: automated emails and Console alerts when a customer enters soft-overage (thresholds at 80% and 100%) and when grace window is about to expire
Telemetry & metrics: per-customer counters, percent of requests served under soft-overage, median enforcement latency, and daily overage revenue estimate
Migration: existing customers retain current hard-limit behavior unless they opt into soft-overage; provide a migration flag in admin API
Admin APIs: endpoints to set quotas, toggle soft-overage, and query current remaining quota and overage state programmatically
Edge cases: support Dedicated/Private deployments where billing events are disabled (soft-overage must be configurable to hard-throttle in those environments)
Audit logging: all changes to quota configuration and enrollment in soft-overage must produce immutable audit events (who, when, what changed)
Safety controls: global kill-switch to disable soft-overage platform-wide for incident response
acceptance_criteria: API returns quota headers and values are consistent across 99% of requests in a 10k request smoke test
Dogfood customers can enable soft-overage and generate overage ledger events consumed by billing ingestion pipeline (validated end-to-end in staging)
Console shows per-customer usage timeline with soft-overage highlighted and links to billing preview; UI passes accessibility and UX review
Notifications fire at 80% and 100% usage thresholds and at T-minus 6 hours before grace window expiration (email and in-console), verified with integration tests
Billing receives signed overage events (schema v1) and matches ingestion contract; end-to-end test produces expected charge preview in billing-qa dashboard
Performance: enforcement path adds <3ms median latency at 95th percentile for token check in the serving runtime under normal traffic
Reliability: system enforces quotas correctly under concurrent requests from same customer (no double-spend) demonstrated by chaos test in staging
Data retention: quota and overage audit events are retained according to compliance policy and visible in audit logs within 5 minutes of change
Fallback: when billing pipeline is unavailable, system queues overage events for up to 72 hours and notifies ops; queued events are replayable without duplication
Migration: at least one pilot customer migrates from hard-limit to soft-overage without support tickets for unexpected charges during the pilot
scope: In-scope: API-level enforcement, admin APIs, billing event generation, Console quota UI, notifications, telemetry, migration flag for existing customers, staging and production rollout plan. Out-of-scope: billing pricing model changes (per-unit price calculation), invoicing workflow redesign, and legal/terms-of-service modifications (these will be coordinated but are separate tickets).
out_of_scope: Per-unit price adjustments, enterprise contract negotiations, marketplace listing changes, deep refunds/process for billing disputes (handled by Ops via separate process).
open_questions: What rounding policy should we use when converting tokens to billing units for tiered plans (round-up, round-down, nearest)?
Should Free-tier customers be opted into soft-overage by default or require explicit opt-in?
How should soft-overage interact with Dedicated/Private customers that have no billing pipeline—should we default to hard-throttle?
What thresholds (80%, 100%) are configurable per plan or must be global defaults for initial release?
Should the grace window be measured in wall time (24h) or rolling usage window?
What rate-limit key granularity do we support initially (customer-level vs. customer+project vs. customer+route)?
decisions: Adopt token-bucket enforcement per (customer, route) with configurable burst tokens — chosen for simplicity and predictable burst behavior
Implement soft-overage as a grace window defaulted to 24 hours for Starter and above; Free-tier remains hard-throttle by default pending legal review
Overage events will be emitted to billing.overages Kafka topic with schema v1; billing team owns ingestion and mapping to invoices
Console will expose a preview of projected overage charges derived from current pricing tables; initially labeled as estimate
Soft-overage must be opt-out for enterprise-managed Dedicated deployments and opt-in for self-serve Hosted customers
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dogfood (Week 1–2): enable for engineering test accounts, validate metrics and billing events. 2) Beta cohort (Week 3–4): invite 10 pilot customers across Free/Starter/Pro to opt-in; collect feedback and monitor support. 3) Opt-in general availability (Week 5): open opt-in toggle in Console and Admin API. 4) GA (Week 8): turn on for all eligible Hosted plans with communications. During each stage run a billing-reconciliation job and weekly postmortem. Rollback strategy: global kill-switch + per-customer revert to hard-limit. Coordinate with Support and Billing for helpdesk playbook.
metrics: monthly overage revenue (USD) attributed to soft-overage
number of support tickets related to unexpected charges per 1k customers
median token-check latency (ms) in enforcement path
percent of requests served while in soft-overage vs blocked
billing ingestion lag (minutes) from overage event emission to visibility in billing system
